intro: Long ago, a race at Olympia had one result: the winner's name. Nobody could say how fast anyone ran. Swimmers raced in the sea, and tennis was played in stone halls with walls. Every place did things its own way.

Over time, people measured these places and wrote the measurements down. A track became 400 meters around. An Olympic pool became 50 meters long. A tennis court became a rectangle 78 feet long. Clubs, federations and the IHSA in Illinois kept the rules and the records.

In this unit you will meet the people who did that work, and the people who were shut out and then let in. You will be able to explain how a lap, a lane and a painted line let a runner, a swimmer or a player in one town compare with someone far away.
bigQuestion: How did measured tracks, pools and courts let people in different places compete fairly?

test.q: What was the only result kept for an ancient Olympic footrace?
test.why: The Greeks had no way to time seconds, so they kept winners' names.

test.q: Which writer doubted the oldest names on the Olympic victor list?
test.why: Plutarch said Hippias had no strong proof for the earliest names.

choices: a festival at Olympia with a girls' footrace
test.why: The Heraia honored Hera and included a race for unmarried girls.

test.q: When was the world track and field body founded?
test.why: It was founded in Stockholm in 1912 and renamed World Athletics in 2019.

test.q: What is a stagger on a track?
choices: starting marks moved ahead in outer lanes
test.why: A stagger evens out the distance for runners in outer lanes.

test.q: Why did hand times vary from timer to timer?
choices: People pressed a little early or late.
test.why: Hand timers are people, so their reactions differ slightly.

test.q: Since 1977, how must world records in short races be timed?
test.why: Electric timing became required for records up to 400 meters in 1977.

test.q: What do IHSA records list from 1893?
test.why: The records list track champions from 1893, before the 1900 founding.

test.q: Who won the first women's Olympic 100 meters?
test.why: Betty Robinson of Riverdale, Illinois, won in 1928.

test.q: Where did the first Paralympic Games take place?
test.why: The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960.

test.q: Where was the first Olympic pool built?
test.why: London built a 100-meter pool in its stadium for the 1908 Games.

test.q: Why were swim times cut to hundredths after 1972?
choices: Lanes can differ by a few millimeters.
test.why: A race won by two thousandths showed that lane lengths can differ more than that.

test.q: What did Walter Wingfield do in 1874?
test.why: Wingfield introduced the game in 1873 and patented it in 1874.

test.q: Why did Black players form the American Tennis Association in 1916?
choices: because most clubs would not let them join
test.why: Most U.S. clubs shut Black players out, so they built their own tournaments.

test.q: When did the IHSA crown its first boys tennis champion?
test.why: The first IHSA boys tennis champion was crowned in 1912.

write.prompt: Which mattered more for fair contests: a measured place (a 400-meter track, a 50-meter pool, a 78-foot court) or a better clock? Use two or three dates or records from this unit, such as the Olympia victor list, the 1908 London pool, the 1972 Munich swim, or IHSA records.
tips: Name each date, record or rule you use, and say where it comes from.
Explain what changed before and after that date.
